recommendation_summary: Wrap the nightly-sync cron invocation on edna so it pings a Healthchecks.io-style dead-man's-switch endpoint on exit, which alerts the user by email or push if the ping is missing or reports failure.

labels.Requirements and who asked: you asked for "I only found out by accident" to stop happening. That means an alert on failure, not a dashboard.
labels.Deleted: centralized logging stack (Loki/Grafana/ELK style) on the Synology — nobody asked for log *browsing*, you asked not to have to look.
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync has no failure signal independent of its own success path (it emails only after finishing). Fix that seam, not storage.
labels.Checked myself: you told me it crashed at startup four nights before the email step, and nothing else alerts on this job today — that's the actual gap.

note: The reply recommends one dead-man alert and rejects the Synology/Docker log stack; leaving 'self-hosted or hosted' to the user is borderline, but self-hosting is not itself recommended and the reply stresses no new host or Docker.
